reasons: Correct party mapping: the audit/inspection right in §3.4 runs against 'the Company' (our party alias), and HDI is the counterparty, so the AUDIT rule is properly triggered and the 'deviation' status is right — the clause has notice/business-hours/cost but no frequency cap, no confidentiality/independent-auditor requirement and no system-access carve-out.

Redline reaches the preferred position: once per 12 months, 30 days' notice (already present), business hours (already present), independent auditor bound by confidentiality, off-site where practicable, and no direct or remote system access; the inserted language is grammatically integrated into the original sentence structure.

Correctly omits the >5% underpayment cost-shift: the existing unconditional 'fees ... shall be borne by HDI' is more favorable than the playbook floor, so not importing the exception is directionally sound rather than rule-incomplete.

Failed 'minimal edit' heuristics (0.63/0.69 changed-character ratio) are explained by the substance of the rule — frequency, auditor-confidentiality and system-access limits cannot be added without appreciable insertions; the original operative terms (notice, business hours, HDI cost) are preserved verbatim.
Comment is accurate, in-house voice, cites the playbook position and offers a sensible fallback (annual on-site records review at HDI's cost).

Minor drafting note for the drafter, not fatal: the absolute bar on access to the Company's 'facilities' sits in slight tension with 'off-site to the extent reasonably practicable' and with the offered on-site fallback; narrowing the exclusion to 'systems and networks' would remove the ambiguity.
